doc.name: cencora world (converted from desmap fixture cencora_v3)

$comment: Converted from sim/desmap/tests/fixtures/cencora_v3.json (WarehouseDesign v3): a 153 x 96 grid at 850 mm, 19 relay zones, one rack prototype, 26 stations, 84 clip boxes, 14 parking zones, 340 HTMs. The old file already records that its row axis is not one pitch: it carries row_centers_mm because the diving boards inside a rack bay sit 645/645/850 apart and no uniform pitch lands on that sequence. Nothing here is laundered back through a uniform pitch to get rid of it — the bays repeat at their true 2,140 mm and each bay's three diving boards sit at their surveyed 425/1070/1715 mm, which reproduces all 18 surveyed row centres exactly, while the open floor keeps a floor pitch and the relays bind its cells many-to-one. The one prototype becomes TWO templates, because which face the boards present on is a fact about the steel now and this site's 38 runs alternate faces across their aisles. Old grid [c, r] -> mm [850c+425, row_centers_mm[r]]. See CONVERSION.md for every mapping decision, what the old file could not say, and what this conversion had to invent.

frame.$comment: The old fixture's grid: 153 wide x 96 deep, cell_size_mm 850, no mirror (desmap fixtures are self-consistent). An old index names a cell, and a cell's place is its centre, so the transform is the formula this file's own header states: index [c,r] reads as millimetres [850c+425, 850r+425] — the 850 mm pitch as the scale, half a cell as the translation. A zero translation would name the cell's minimum corner instead, and shift every projection half a cell into the next square. Declared for projection only — nothing below is positioned in it — and this fixture is the proof that the projection is nominal and lossy (SPEC §4). Column centres do land on 850c+425 everywhere. Row centres do NOT: the old file carries row_centers_mm because grid rows 20-37 are the surveyed relay positions of the rack runs (645/645/850 repeating), and everything above them is shifted a constant -2460 mm off the nominal lattice, because 18 rows of true relay pitch span 12,840 mm where 18 nominal cells would span 15,300 mm.

tiling.$comment: 153 x 20 = 3060 cells on the nominal lattice, which for these rows IS the survey: grid rows 0-19 sit at 850c+425 exactly. The pick stations and their queues live here. No flow is declared, so the band compiles two_way (SPEC §5: flow restricts, never permits) — the old fixture has zero highways and lets HTMs roam the open grid.

entities.name: open floor: lane past bay 1 (grid rows 20-22)

tiling.$comment: The HTM lane running past one bay of the rack faces. The old file gives these rows at 645/645/850, and that is the survey: the three diving-board positions inside a 2,140 mm bay, six bays deep, which desmap had to bend its single row axis onto because it has one pitch per axis for everything. This rectangle keeps them — three rows at the boards' own 645 mm — so a cell centre stands under every board and each relay binds a cell of its own. That is why one bay is one rectangle: 645 tiles a bay exactly and no single pitch tiles the run, and a lane retiled at a pitch of its own leaves relays sharing cells sideways, which SPEC §5 calls a misalignment. The origin sits half a step low so that 645's half-step centre rounds half-up onto the surveyed number. Centres: 17425, 18070, 18715. Nothing is minted alongside: the cell an HTM stands on to work a board is a cell of the lane it was already driving.

exclusions.$comment: zone 1 footprint: The whole three-column zone leaves the floor: both rack columns and the VTM aisle between them, 3 x 15 = 45 relay-band cells per zone. The old compiler kept the aisle as CellKind::Aisle, blocked every HTM edge touching one, and walled the column at both ends with clip boxes — so no HTM ever entered it, and VTMs need no floor cells at all, because the rack is their habitat (SPEC §7). What used to be an aisle column is now the 850 mm of clear air between two rack footprints that face away from each other.

tiling.$comment: 153 x 58 = 8874 cells at uniform 850 pitch again, but anchored at y = 29,840 rather than the nominal 32,300: the surveyed band below is 2,460 mm shorter than 18 nominal cells, and every row above it inherits that shift. The 16 putaway stations live here, as does the building notch — the single 114 x 46 clip box that removes 5,244 of these cells.

exclusions.$comment: clip 0: All 84 clip_boxes of the old file, in source order, one exclusion each and no further comment on any of them — a clip box is an anonymous 'make this Blank' rectangle with no id and no reason attached, and this is what 84 of them look like. This first one carries most of the work: 114 x 46 grid cells, the corner of the bounding rectangle that is not the building — cencora's floor is an L. Ten of the 84 are exact duplicates of another (the zone-end walls at columns 82, 100 and 107), harmless in both formats. Each rectangle's y range is cut midway to the neighbouring row centres, so it strictly contains the centres it means to remove and none of its neighbours' (SPEC §5).

stitch.$comment: The seam where the uniform lattice hands over to the first bay's lane: 102 mm of gap, columns aligned, one link per surviving column pair. Nothing links without a stitch (SPEC §5) — two bands that abut are two bands that abut.

cencora A5 bay (4 slot columns x 11 shelves, 3 relays) (relays on the +y face)

template.$comment: One bay of the old racks[] prototype 'cencora_a5_bay', presenting its boards on the '+y' face. The old file had one prototype and said nothing about faces; v0.6 puts the relay face on the steel, so a prototype whose copies present opposite ways is two templates. That is what this conversion found and it is not a defect of either format: desmap could not say which way a board pointed, and the runs on the two sides of an aisle genuinely point opposite ways. The template still takes no parameters, and which class works the STORAGE face, from where, still belongs to the access each run declares.

rack.$comment: Pure steel, as one enumerated list of level heights bottom-up: two relay levels at 394 and 952 mm, then the eleven shelves the old prototype surveyed, 1580 mm up to 7577 mm. That shelf sequence is a 558/559 mm rhythm with two 764 mm structural jumps in it, which is why the list states each height instead of asserting a pitch no shelf sits on. The two relay levels are what the old format could not say at all — it had one relay per position and no heights — and each states where its three shelves stand on the bay, as [along the run, out across it], plus how far one may reach for a cell. The 'out' number is which side of the steel they present on, said as geometry: 850 is the far edge of the bay's depth on this face, 0 the near edge on the other. Six relays per bay, addressed 'relay:{level},{i}'; the two levels at one position share the cell an HTM stands on, because a stack is two shelves and one place to stand, and they share it without being told to: both find the same nearest cell. Which face the STORAGE is worked from, and by whom, is not here: that is the access, declared per zone, because this same steel is served from outside by an HTM and from inside by a climbing A5.

stamp.$comment: Old zone 1: type relay, origin [146, 20], length 18, sides Dual (the default), 6 Left + 6 Right bays at x_offset 0, 2140, ... 10700. The zone's three grid columns are rack / VTM aisle / rack; this stamp is the LEFT rack column. The template runs along its own +x and the heading turns it to run along world +y, so the repeat marches 2,140 mm a bay, six bays, 17,000 -> 29,840 mm. The repeat is legitimate here because the BAY pitch is genuinely uniform: the 645/645/850 alternation the old grid needed row_centers_mm for is the three relay offsets inside one bay, and it comes out of the relay levels' positions at true millimetres — 17425, 18070, 18715, 19565, ... exactly the 18 surveyed row centres. This run takes the '+y'-face template, which the 90 degree turn points at world -x, away from the aisle and onto the HTM lane.

The other face of old zone 1, in the grid column on the far side of the aisle. Same pose convention, same heading, same repeat — what differs is the template: this run takes the '-y'-face copy, which after the quarter turn points at world +x, again away from the aisle. Through v0.5 both runs stamped one template and the face rode on each run's own boards-access; now the face is on the steel, so the two directions are two templates. Keeping the heading the same for both is what keeps bay 0 at the same end of the run on both sides of the aisle.

sector.$comment: One sector per old zone, not per zone group: vtm_count is a per-zone number in the old file, so the thing a VTM cohort is hard-assigned to has to be the zone. The two members are the zone's two rack rows; a generator member stands for its whole expansion, so this names both faces, all 12 bays, and every relay and slot beneath them.

station.$comment: Old station 1: station_type Pick, position [13, 0], presentation_cell [13, 1], queue_path [[10,1], [11,1], [12,1]], exit_direction East. Ten of these sit along grid row 0 with a straight three-cell approach in row 1. exit_direction maps by desmap's own definition (sim/desmap/src/design/queue_edges.rs: North is (0,-1) in [col, row], South (0,+1)), and row centres increase with y in both formats, so North is -y and East is +x.

entities.$comment: Old presentation_cell [13, 1]: the floor's own derived cell GAINS a presentation_point by override, keeping its pose and traversability, with an `expect` pin on where the author believes that ordinal address sits. All 26 stations are decorated this way.

station.$comment: Old station 11: station_type Putaway, position [13, 47], presentation_cell [12, 47], exit_direction North. The queue is a five-cell horseshoe — down column 11, across, and back up column 12 — the same point-of-no-return shape the EasyLoop's queue has, drawn here in plain floor cells. The old file's settings.putaway.queue_depth of 2 is a scenario admission limit and is parked with the other settings.

robot_class.$comment: The old file's entire robot model is fleet.htms = 340. Footprint and height are representative placeholders. The speed is the one number the source does carry, settings.htm.empty_speed = 4.5, read as m/s — the old settings block states no unit. No 'lineage': the source names no maker for this class, and a lineage names organizations, so this conversion asserts none rather than putting a placeholder where a company's name goes.

entities.name: VTM A5

robot_class.$comment: Model A5 is the one thing the old map says about a VTM (VtmModel::A5, the zone default). 'height' is the zone's declared zone_height_mm of 10,017 — the racking height the VTM's vertical travel spans, which is the closest the old format comes to a robot dimension. Footprint is a representative placeholder. Cycle times (pick 6.2 s, drop 5.0 s, alignment 3.0 s) are settings and are parked.

entities.$comment: One machine, two names, and in v0.6 that is a lineage rather than a legacy identifier: Quicktron manufactures the A5, Dematic distributes it as the DA50, and the chain runs origin first. Through v0.5 the rebrand rode in external_ids beside the desmap ids, which was the wrong shelf — external_ids holds join keys into systems that already exist, and 'what Dematic sells this as' is a live commercial fact with a party and a role behind it (SPEC §2, §10.1). Neither name is in the source file: desmap says VtmModel::A5 and nothing else, so the two parties are an invention of this conversion and are listed as one in CONVERSION.md. locomotion 'ladder' is what makes the inner aisles untiled — this class climbs the racking and never stands on the ground, so there is no floor to give it.

cohort.$comment: Old fleet.htms: 340. They roam the open floor; nothing pins them to a zone.

Old zone.vtm_count, unset in every cencora zone and therefore the default 2 — 19 zones, 38 VTMs, a number that existed nowhere in the old file and had to be summed out of the map. Hard-assigned to the zone's sector: these two never leave it.

carrier_type.$comment: Implicit in the old format — no carrier type exists there. Dimensions are representative. scenario.units_per_tote = 1 is a workload fact and is parked.

region.$comment: The 2,550 mm zone footprint is rack (850) + aisle (850) + rack (850); this is the middle strip, running the full length of the steel. It declares NO tiling, and that is the point: the A5 that works these faces climbs the racking, so there is no floor here for anybody to stand on and inventing cells would put a lane in the graph that no robot drives. Tiling follows locomotion (SPEC §5). The old fixture had no way to say any of this — the aisle existed only as the gap left by an exclusion.

access.$comment: The junction between this run and the region it is worked from, and the only access the run needs: the inward face, onto the aisle between the two runs. It derives nothing — the climb is rack-internal motion — but it is what makes this zone somewhere the A5 works, which is how the zone's cohort keeps its habitat now that a rack is no longer habitat by itself. It is also where slot depth counts from. The outward face is not a second access any more: it is the 'face' on the steel's relay levels, and the cell an HTM stands on is whichever lane cell each relay reaches.
